analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a 'Download completion ownership' section (head lines 44-53). That section documents running StreamingFileDownloadDelegateTests. The tests cancel a suspended URLSession task before attaching a waiter, check both completion orders and duplicate terminal callbacks, race attachment against completion, and verify that cancellation preserves the exact .part bytes. The text says fixtures use unique temporary directories and never resume a network task or load weights, and that these component tests do not qualify live HTTP downloads or model serving.

This is documentation only. It adds no runtime code, no new endpoints, no trust-boundary change and no new environment variables or secrets. It does not weaken any control in the threat model (TB-002/TB-003/TB-007, T-012 weights, T-041 cache, A-004 model weights). It makes no new qualification claim, and it states a limit on what the tests prove. The rest of the document (units 5 and 6) appears as unchanged context. I looked in it for instructions that would loosen isolation, such as pointing tests at production or reusing a live provider's cache. The existing text keeps requiring isolated state, exclusive GPU use, ephemeral or isolated keys, and never using production cache roots or keys. The patch changes none of that. I identified no regression.

Remaining question for integration: the StreamingFileDownloadDelegate implementation, which handles download completion and .part file handling, is not in this batch. Whether the download path preserves weight-hash verification (T-012/T-027) is therefore unverified here and is outside this docs-only change.
